summary: Checked all three added docs (`builder` field, `readResolve`, `writeReplace`) against their implementations in DefaultSerializationProxy.scala: builder's role matches readObject/readResolve usage, readResolve's description matches builder.result() and the standard readResolve serialization hook semantics, and writeReplace's description matches the factory-selecting pattern match and `new DefaultSerializationProxy(f, this)` construction. No false or misleading claims found; two minor nits noted.

items.issue: First sentence is 'Creates a serialization proxy for this collection.' rather than starting with 'Returns', so per the house @return-drop rule an @return tag is technically warranted, though the first sentence already conveys the return value (the created proxy) clearly enough that omission is not misleading.
items.suggestion: Either reword the first sentence to 'Returns a serialization proxy for this collection.' or add `@return the DefaultSerializationProxy that replaces this collection during serialization`.

items.issue: All three newly-written doc comments follow the same second-sentence pattern ('This builder is initialized...', 'This method is called automatically...', 'This method is called during serialization...'), which reads mechanically when viewed together.
items.suggestion: Vary the phrasing of the elaboration sentence across the three comments if revising for other reasons; not worth a standalone edit otherwise.
